summary: Dancing with SAR is an interactive geospatial and spatiotemporal visualization platform designed to track, analyze, and communicate changes occurring across Earth's surface using Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) observations from the NASA-ISRO NISAR mission. Developed around the Earth Twin Engine (ETE) architecture and its TerraTrace scientific subsystem, the platform transforms complex microwave radar backscatter, polarization, and phase measurements into accessible visual representations. It addresses the limitations of traditional optical satellites—which are frequently blinded by thick cloud cover and darkness—by enabling robust, all-weather environmental monitoring. The application allows users to explore selected geographic regions, examine radar observations acquired at different points in time, compare surface conditions through a generalized timeline, and visualize environmental changes such as flood inundation, forest degradation, wetland fluctuations, and ground deformation.
details:
Dancing with SAR organizes satellite radar observations into a continuous spatiotemporal representation of Earth's changing surface rather than treating them as isolated static images. The core workflow encompasses study area selection, NISAR data acquisition from NASA Earthdata/ASF DAAC, data preparation and spatial registration, chronological timeline organization, and scientific change detection. By coupling an interactive 3D Earth visualization interface with a generalized timeline and a delta backscatter change-detection engine ($\Delta B(x,y,t) = B(x,y,t_2) - B(x,y,t_1)$), the system highlights locations where radar responses have significantly shifted over time.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

  • All-Weather Monitoring: Overcomes optical weather barriers (clouds, storms, night) using active microwave signals.
  • Decision Support: Empowers Earth scientists, disaster-management authorities, agricultural researchers, and affected communities to visualize both where environmental changes occur and how they evolve over time.
  • Multidisciplinary Applications: Initial focus areas include flood inundation mapping, wetland and forest disturbance tracking, agricultural surface changes, and surface deformation analysis.

Tech Stack, Tools, & Architecture Reuse:

  • Reused ETE Infrastructure: Preserves established frontend application logic, backend runtime core, 3D globe visualization rendering pipeline, geographic coordinate handling, and generalized timeline infrastructure originally explored in Avani.
  • New TerraTrace Subsystem Components: Implements domain-specific NISAR data adapters supporting HDF5, GeoTIFF, and NetCDF formats, metadata interpreters, raster preparation and radiometric normalization pipelines, and temporal comparison change-detection engines.
  • Languages & Ecosystem: Python, JavaScript, React.js, geospatial raster libraries, and web-based 3D graphics rendering modules.
